page.layout: Running head at top, page number at top right; one column of running text; below it a woodcut ornament band; then the chapter heading (CAP. LXXVIII. with title) and an italic argument summary with a large woodcut initial; signature A.iiij. at lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: que esse, qui etiam ante hunc cōditus sit à Deo. Quæ sententia huic, quem nunc exponimus, errori, magnum firmamentum videtur attulisse, & tamen falsa est. In principio enim creauit Deus cœlum & terram, nec antea vllus mundus erat vel visibilis vel inuisibilis. Nec tunc Deus mundos plures condidit, sed hunc tantum conspicuum, quem incolimus, cuiúsque nobis Genef.cap.1. origo explicatur. Et rectè Patres argumentantur vnum esse mundum, quia vnus est Deus. Est enim opus Dei mundus. Neque verò prætermissura erat Scriptura, si plures essent mundi, ne alium præter vnum & verum Deum, eorum conditorem existimaremus: aut ne Deũ ipsum tanti opificij laude priuaremus. De quo in prima Physicæ nostræ Christianæ parte, quæ tamen nondum edita est, abūdè diximus. Quod autem ad hanc hæresin attinet, neque illius originem, neque durationem, neque sedem vsquam legimus. Huius tamen breuissimè quidem meminit Isidorus, & fuit minuta hæresis, quę magnos authores aut patronos diuturnámque ætatem habuisse minimè mihi videtur, eám que ad Basilidianos refero.
main_text.head: CAP. LXXVIII. Tertullii & eorum error quis fuerit.

head.i: Lia[?] fceleratorum animas{1} conuerti in dæmonas dicit, & in qnaque animalia suis meritis congrua.

page.notes: Large woodcut initial at the start of the argument is unclear; read as "L" with [?]. The word "qnaque" is doubtful (possibly quæque with an abbreviation). The reference mark {1} after "animas" has no matching footnote on this page. The long s is transcribed as plain s throughout. Printed "conspicuum" appears as "confpicuum" in the scan and has been normalised to the Latin spelling as the only change, along with u/v and i/j. The chapter heading and argument are set in capitals and italics as printed.
